note: The original is in German, extracted from the OCR text of a library scan at the Internet Archive (archive.org item biostor-232733); some figures and letters are misread and were checked against the context and the plate legends; figures that could not be confirmed are omitted. The original description includes the soldier and worker; it gives no nesting details, only the nest shape and the habitat in primary forest.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 3.8 mm, head length 1.62 mm, head width 0.88 mm, frontal process length 0.66 mm. Head yellowish brown to rusty yellow, the frontal process rusty brown; head with a few longer bristles and densely covered with microscopic bristles or spinules; tip of the frontal process covered with short bristles; abdominal sclerites weakly rusty brown, the rest pale straw-yellow; tergites with short decumbent hairs and a few long bristles at the posterior margin; venter more strongly hairy with more bristles. Head (Plate W1) oval, the frontal process long and narrow; frontal outline straight with a small elevation in the middle. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 2. Anterior margin of the pronotum raised; body of uniform width.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 3.9 mm, head length 1.08 mm, head width 0.9 mm. Head rusty yellow or rusty brown, the cephalic sutures pale and narrow, the transverse suture uneven; head finely hairy with a few long bristles; tergites and sternites pale rusty yellow; sternites finely hairy, the posterior margins of both dorsal and ventral sclerites (especially ventral) with a few long bristles. Frons (Plate X1b) with a large oval fontanelle; clypeus convex, the sclerite concave in the middle and lens-shaped, the tip inconspicuous; labrum ligulate; basal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior, the anterior margin with small teeth; basal tooth of the left mandible with 2 points.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The species inhabits primary forest and builds conical (sugar-loaf) nests. Locality: Creveaux, Chaco, Bolivia (collected by Nordenskiöld in 1902).
